beats.narration: The death notification lands in the Onboarding inbox with a certified death certificate and IDs for Robert and his sister Lily.
Olivia's agent gently extracts the notification — Mei's pension CP-3019042 ($486,200), the death certificate and both children's IDs — and stops the pension payments.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261113-OPS005 and asks Theo to own it personally.
Theo takes ownership of the case for compassionate oversight — every message to the family is reviewed by a person.
Felix checks the death certificate and both beneficiaries' IDs for authenticity — all genuine ✓.
Ben reviews Mei's binding death benefit nomination against SIS reg 6.17A and the trust deed.

Ben: BDBN signed 18 Mar 2024 before two adult non-beneficiary witnesses ✓, valid until 18 Mar 2027 ✓, Robert 50% and Lily 50% — both SIS dependants ✓. It is binding: the trustee must pay as nominated.
Ivy redeems Mei's pension portfolio to cash and notes that the final amounts depend on market movements until the units are sold.
Ben hands the case to Payments with the 50/50 beneficiary split.

Penny calculates each payment: gross $243,100 — tax-free $92,378, taxable $150,722, 17% withheld ($25,622.74) — and pays $217,477.26 to each child once Theo approves the Microsoft Teams card (every death benefit needs Team Leader approval).
Cara sends Robert and Lily gentle condolence letters explaining the tax, the timeline and their complaint rights (IDR, then AFCA).

result.headline: Benefit paid — Mum's wishes followed
result.summary: Outcome: COMPLETED — $486,200 paid 50/50 to Robert and Lily under Mei's binding nomination ($217,477.26 net each)
